LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NONVERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.6: Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you do to pronounce words clearly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source
2. show interest in speaking activities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NONVERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NONVERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source

What this means
In this part you learn to imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show interest in speaking activities

What this means
In this part you learn to show interest in speaking activities. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show interest in speaking activities.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show interest in speaking activities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement to a partner. (skill: show interest in speaking activities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.
3. Practise this skill: show interest in speaking activities.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do to pronounce words clearly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative speaking Repetition Nonverbal communication Intonation Engagement means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.
5. Be able to: show interest in speaking activities.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
